Part 1

What does a block flow diagram show, and do its streams balance?

Part 1 · the plan

Blocks, numbered streams, balances

  1. Three drawings, three jobsblock flow diagram, process flow diagram, piping and instrument diagram
  2. The blocks and their streamstwelve blocks, sixteen numbered streams
  3. Boundary balancesin − out = accumulation, around four boundaries
  4. What the control system can closewhich balances the plant's own meters can check

Interactive · pick a drawing

Block flow diagram (BFD), process flow diagram (PFD), P&ID

Each drawing adds detail for a later decision: concept, then balances and sizing, then construction and safety reviews.

The block flow diagram of T-101 and its vacuum system

Sixteen numbered streams carry every flow across a block boundary; the numbers are the model's design state.

What each block does, and which streams it joins

A block hides its pumps, valves and instruments: only what crosses its boundary is drawn.

Interactive · pick a boundary

Four balances at the design point

The same sum around four boundaries: two of mass, one of inert gas, one of heat.

Every balance closes: the column gap is 0.0004 % of the feed, the drum and sump still settling.

Interactive · move the feed, the model runs 30 min

A balance during a change: the accumulation term

Column boundary$\dot m_1-\dot m_4-\dot m_5-\dot m_7=dM/dt$

After a feed step the drum and sump fill: in ≠ out until the levels settle, and the gap is the accumulation.

Interactive · pick a balance

Which balances the distributed control system (DCS) can check

Column mass and heat close from meters; the ejector package and the air leak need the model or a field test.

Part 1 · summary

What part 1 settled

  • The BFD shows blocks, numbered streams and battery limits, nothing more.
  • Sixteen streams carry every flow across a block boundary.
  • In − out = accumulation closes around each boundary at design.
  • Meters close the column balances; the ejector package needs the model.
2

Part 2

What does the PFD add, and how do its numbered streams and flags read?

Part 2 · the plan

Reading drawing VD-PFD-001

  1. What a PFD addsequipment symbols and tags, defining valves, flags
  2. The drawingsixteen items, thirty-two streams on one A4 sheet
  3. Streams and flagsflow, temperature and pressure where the model has them
  4. Unit balances on PFD numberseach item closes on the flags around it
  5. Flags against the running plantthe drawing is one operating point

From blocks to equipment

What a PFD adds, and what it still leaves out

Adds

Every item by symbol and tag. Every stream numbered. Flags: flow, temperature, pressure. The defining control valves. Utilities named.

Leaves out

Line sizes and specifications. Isolation, drain and vent valves. Relief devices. Most instrument loops.

Interactive · zoom and pan the sheet

VD-PFD-001 Rev 0, issued for teaching

One A4 sheet holds sixteen items and thirty-two streams; zoom to read a flag box.

Interactive · step through the PFD streams

Each flag against the model's design state

20 of 32 streams carry flags; every flag matches the model to its last printed digit.

Interactive · pick an item

Each item closes on the flags around it

At steady state$\sum\dot m_{in}=\sum\dot m_{out}$

The five vacuum-package items close exactly; the hotwell passes 149 kg/h of condensate to waste water.

Reading the pressure flags in order

Pressure along the gas path

Two ejector stages lift 6.85 to 110 kPa a, ratios 3.75 and 4.28; the vent then drops to atmosphere.

Interactive · change the boil-up, the model runs 30 min

The drawing is one operating point

Design 1.655 t/h. Red: the value has moved more than 2 % from the sheet.

More boil-up moves the column flags; the ejector flags hardly move, because the vacuum system sees only the vent gas.

Part 2 · summary

What part 2 settled

  • The PFD draws every item, numbers every stream and flags the model values.
  • Twenty flagged streams; each item closes on the flags around it.
  • The gas path reads 7.00 → 6.85 → 25.7 → 110 kPa a.
  • The sheet is one operating point; the running plant moves away from it.

Part 3

How does each drawing grow into the next, and do the drawings agree?

Part 3 · the plan

BFD → PFD → P&ID

  1. One BFD stream, several PFD streamspumps and valves split a block stream
  2. One block, many itemsthe vacuum block opened up
  3. What the P&ID addsevery line, valve and instrument loop
  4. Drawings must agreechecks that found real differences

Interactive · pick a BFD stream

Which PFD streams each BFD stream becomes

The PFD keeps the BFD numbers in a column of its own: the link between the sheets.

Pumps, tees and valves split one block stream into a chain of PFD streams with the same flow.

Interactive · zoom into the P&ID

VD-PID-201 Rev B: the ejector package

The P&ID adds every valve, instrument and interlock: the drawing the plant is built and operated from.

From process to plant

What the P&ID adds to the PFD

Instruments

Every transmitter, controller and alarm with its tag and loop.

Valves

Isolation, drain, vent and check valves; hand valves.

Lines

Line numbers, sizes and piping specifications.

Protection

Relief devices and the safety instrumented system (SIS).

Interactive · pick a check

Cross-checks that found real differences

Each drawing is checked against the model and the other drawings; a difference is fixed in the next revision.

Part 3 · summary

What part 3 settled

  • A BFD stream becomes a chain of PFD streams with the same flow.
  • A block opens into items, valves and the start-up equipment.
  • The P&ID adds every line, valve, instrument and protection layer.
  • Cross-checks between drawings and the model find real errors.

This deck

Key Takeaways

1

Use the BFD for scope and the overall balance.

2

Number every stream; close every boundary on those numbers.

3

Read PFD flags as one operating point, not the plant now.

4

Carry stream numbers from BFD to PFD to P&ID.

5

Cross-check drawings against each other and the model.
